newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber weak as weather pressures cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber weak as weather pressures cash.

text.p: Reduced demand for cash lumber due to poor weather conditions through much of the United States weighed on CME lumber futures early, traders said.

The weak tone to cash lumber weighed on futures from the start. However, underlying support was still evident on expectations that demand for wood would improve once the weather improves, traders said.

Cash sources said bitter cold and snowy weather has dampened demand for wood and wholesalers dropped asking prices another $5 to $6 per tbf overnight to the $380 to $385 area. This compares with Wednesday's official quote of $400.
At 0935 CST, lumber posted losses of $2.40 to $0.70 per tbf with March off most at $407.90 and May off $0.70 at $381.80 per tbf.
